title: Upper Deck Seat Track Corrosion Protection by Sealed Track Sections
abstract: Sealed seat track sections in the wet areas of the upper deck floor, introduced to arrest filiform and pitting corrosion under the galleys and lavatories on early aircraft.

sections.reason: Early TITAN aircraft entering their first heavy checks showed corrosion along the upper deck seat tracks wherever the track passed under a galley or a lavatory. Twenty-two aircraft were affected in the first three years, with pitting depths of up to 0.4 mm and filiform attack extending several track pitches either side of the wet area. The corrosion did not affect load capability at the depths found but it made seat leg removal difficult and, on four aircraft, required a track section to be cut out and replaced under an engineering repair.
sections.description: The open-section seat track in the affected bays is replaced by a track section web ARD386097-40 carrying an integral elastomeric seal along the fastener line, so that fluid entering the track cannot reach the fastener holes or the underlying floor beam flange. The lower web sub-assembly D5350129109541 is removed with the old track and is not reused. Clevis pins LN666073-13 are used at the track splice positions, which are moved 60 mm outboard of their previous location so that the splice no longer sits under the galley drip path. Drainage at the seat track is redirected to the existing floor drain by a moulded channel bonded to the track flange. The work is done from above with the cabin monuments and the floor panels removed in zones 242 and 265; the floor beams themselves are not disturbed. Revised detail is on drawing D53501208297.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 11.4 kg per aircraft on a full upper deck installation, symmetric about the centre line. No electrical load change. The sealed track sections are not interchangeable with the original open sections because the fastener pitch at the splice differs, so a bay must be converted in full. The repeat detailed visual inspection of the upper deck wet areas is retained at a lengthened interval. Illustrated parts content for the seat track installation requires update, and the cabin monument removal tasks are affected by the revised splice position.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only, on aircraft delivered before the sealed track became the build standard. Embodiment takes about eight days and is normally combined with a cabin refresh, since the monuments have to come out anyway. Kits are ordered by bay rather than by aircraft.

type_data.production_impact: No production cut-in; the sealed section was already the build standard from MSN T00131

issue.reason: Supersession by the titanium attachment fitting standard declared, with the re-machining required on bays that already carry a sealed section.

Operators that have not started should go to the fitting standard directly.
